extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students in humor studies, cognitive psychology, psycholinguistics, and discourse/semantics
extracted.subtask_description: Operationalizing and empirically testing a domains-interaction model of humor that quantifies incongruity and resolution in simple metaphor-like jokes using semantic-distance measures. The work is about designing stimuli, measuring semantic distances, and relating those distances to perceived funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity (between-domain semantic distance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity is operationalized as between-domain semantic distance — the semantic distance between the target term's domain and the domain of the analogy/source. Humor ratings of jokes were positively correlated with incongruity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure between-domain distance via semantic-differential ratings between terms; greater between-domain distance predicts higher humor ratings. Example stimulus form: 'A is the B of A's domain' (e.g., 'John Candy is the hamburger of actors'). Use many term-pairs (the study used 26 terms in 250 jokes) to derive reliable distance estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution (within-domain semantic distance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution is operationalized as within-domain semantic distance — the semantic closeness among items within the same domain that allows reconciliation of the incongruity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure within-domain distance via semantic-differential ratings. In this research resolution alone was not positively correlated with humor ratings, though it plays a role in combination with incongruity (see interaction). Operationalizing resolution precisely is necessary to test its role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of incongruity and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The combination (interaction) of incongruity and resolution is crucial: jokes that possess both substantial incongruity (between-domain distance) and sufficient resolution (within-domain distance) are rated as most humorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test for statistical interaction effects rather than only main effects. The study found a significant interaction such that high incongruity combined with adequate resolution produced the highest humor ratings; this pattern was replicated in a second study. Thus design stimuli and analyses to detect interaction effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke stimulus structure — 'A is the B of A's domain' (simple metaphor-like jokes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use simple, structured sentences of the form 'A is the B of A's domain' to create stimuli that can be analyzed for between- and within-domain distances (e.g., 'John Candy is the hamburger of actors').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This controlled, formulaic structure allows precise operationalization of domains and distances. Use a large, varied set of such items to enable robust semantic-distance calculation and statistical testing across stimuli.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement method: semantic-differential ratings to derive distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Semantic distances (both between-domain and within-domain) are derived from semantic-differential ratings collected for the relevant terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect perceptual/semantic ratings from participants on semantic dimensions and compute distances between terms; ensure sufficient sample size and psychometric reliability. The paper used these derived distances as the independent variables predicting humor ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between humor perception and metaphor appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor perception and metaphor appreciation differ in their relations to semantic distances: when the same sentences are presented as metaphors and rated for aptness, the pattern differs (main effects for both semantic distances but no interaction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing experiments or evaluating stimuli, treat metaphor aptness and humor/funniness as distinct dependent variables; expect different patterns (interaction for humor, additive main effects for metaphor aptness). This implies different evaluative criteria depending on whether the goal is humor or metaphorical aptness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical replication and statistical testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings should be tested across studies and replicated; the paper reports replication of the interaction effect in a second study and a contrasting pattern in a third study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design multiple studies or follow-up replications to confirm effects. Use appropriate statistical tests to assess main effects and interactions between semantic-distance measures and relate them to humor ratings.
